findings.obs_text: In Dan 4:34 lifted (H5191) stands three words before reason: Nebuchadnezzar lifted his eyes to heaven and his reason returned, two clauses in sequence joined by and; the lifting comes first.
In Act 28:20 asked (G3870) stands two words after the phrase for this reason, which governs it: the cause comes first and the asking to see them follows from it.
findings.grounds: I have asked to see you

findings.obs_text: In 1Pe 3:15 the reason (G3056) is what is asked for: asks (G0154) stands two words before it, and the one who asks seeks an account of the hope.
findings.grounds: anyone who asks you for a reason

findings.obs_text: In Act 19:9 unbelief (G0544) stands ten words before reasoning: some continued in unbelief, and so he withdrew and took the disciples with him to reason elsewhere; the unbelief of the hearers is what moves the reasoning to the hall of Tyrannus.

In 1Th 3:5, 1Th 3:7 and 1Ti 1:16 the phrase for this reason points ahead to a clause whose object or means is faith: Paul sends to learn of their faith, their faith is the means of the comfort, and the mercy is shown as a pattern for future believers.
In Pro 3:30 harm (H7451C) stands four words after for no reason, in the clause that gives the ground for it: the man has done no harm, so to contend with him is without cause.
findings.grounds: when he has done you no harm

findings.obs_text: In Num 18:32 profane (H2490H) stands in the next sentence, not joined to by reason of it: the reason phrase frees the giver from sin, and the warning not to profane the holy things follows as its own command.
findings.grounds: you shall not profane the holy things

findings.obs_text: In Dan 4:34 blessed (H1289) stands three words after reason, in the clause that follows its return: once his reason is back, the king blesses the Most High.
findings.grounds: and I blessed the Most High

findings.obs_text: In Act 19:8 boldly (G3955) stands directly before reasoning: he spoke boldly, reasoning and persuading them, so the reasoning is part of the bold speaking in the synagogue.
findings.grounds: spoke boldly, reasoning and persuading them

findings.obs_text: In Act 28:18 liberty (G0630G) stands three words before reason: the wish to release Paul rests on the absence of any cause for a death sentence.
findings.grounds: they wished to set me at liberty

older.reason: it states what Act 28:18-19 tell: the wish to release Paul was overruled by the objection of the Jews, and he appealed to Caesar; a statement of the verses, not of the inner being

findings.obs_text: In Jam 3:17 pure (G0053) stands four places before open to reason in one list of the qualities of the wisdom from above: pure comes first, and open to reason follows after then, peaceable and gentle; they are joined only by the list.
In Jos 5:4 war (H4421) stands ten words after reason, in the explanation the reason introduces: the fighting men who left Egypt died on the way, and that is why Joshua circumcised the people.
findings.grounds: all the men of war, had died in the wilderness

findings.obs_text: In 1Th 3:7 comforted (G3870) stands eight words after for this reason, which governs it: the cause comes first and being comforted about them follows from it.
findings.grounds: we have been comforted about you

findings.obs_text: In 1Sa 20:29 commanded (H6680) stands nine words before for this reason, inside the excuse it sums up: the brother's command to be at the sacrifice is part of the cause given for the absence. The data holds a second code at the same place, H1931 (he), joined to the verb.
findings.grounds: my brother has commanded me to be there

findings.obs_text: In Dan 4:34 praised (H7624) stands five words after reason, among the acts of worship that follow its return: blessing, praising and honoring the one who lives forever.
In Jam 3:17 gentle (G1933) stands directly before open to reason, the next quality in the list of the wisdom from above.
In 1Pe 3:15 gentleness (G4240) stands six words after reason and gives the manner of giving it: the defense for the hope is to be made with gentleness and respect.
findings.grounds: do it with gentleness and respect

older.finding: in 1Pe 3:14-16 what is forbidden (fear of them) and what is asked (gentleness and respect, the Lord as one's fear) stand close together
older.reason: it reads the fear words of 1Pe 3; the fear collection owns it

older.finding: the forbidding of fear and the asking of gentleness and respect stand two verses apart in 1Pe 3
older.reason: it reads the fear words of 1Pe 3; the fear collection owns it, and judges it against 12651, which says nearly the same

older.finding: gentleness as the spirit of a manner of approach (1Co 4:21)
older.reason: it states how gentleness works as a manner of approach; the gentleness words are of the compassion collection

findings.obs_text: In 1Pe 3:15 always (G0104) stands seven words before reason and qualifies the readiness to give it: the believer is to be ready at all times with a defense for the hope.
findings.grounds: always being prepared to make a defense

findings.obs_text: In Dan 4:34 and 1Ti 1:16 the words of lasting time qualify other nouns, not the reason: the everlasting dominion of God, and eternal life at the end of the purpose clause.
